leo_support: FYI customer reporting recurring 502s from POST /v1/generate and occasional 401s. They provided a request id and a tiny curl but need tidy SDK snippets and instructions to collect a debug bundle. Account: acct_9231. Request id seen: req_8a7f9c2b. Can we get minimal Python/JS/Go repros + steps to gather server logs and trace?

anya_engineer: Roger. Can you paste the exact curl you have? Also ask the customer to include the X-Request-Id header in their calls if possible, and to run with a short retry loop so we can reproduce transient 502 vs auth. I'll draft snippets.

leo_support: Here's the curl they originally ran (redacted API key):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hello","max_tokens":10}' \  -v
```

They also included this header in logs: X-Request-Id: req_8a7f9c2b. Response snippet: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":"upstream error","request_id":"req_8a7f9c2b"}
Sometimes the same call returned HTTP/1.1 401 {"error":"invalid_api_key"} with same req id.

anya_engineer: Thanks. Minimal repros below — ask the customer to replace $API_KEY and run each once; they should paste back the exact request id if it differs. Also ask them to set LOG_LEVEL=debug for the SDK/cli to collect client-side logs.

Python (requests):
```
import os
import requests

API_KEY = os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
url = 'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate'
headers = {
    'Authorization': f'Bearer {API_KEY}',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'X-Request-Id': 'req_8a7f9c2b'
}
json = {"model": "gpt-small", "input": "hello", "max_tokens": 10}
resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=json)
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
```

Node.js (fetch):
```
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
const API_KEY = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY
;
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-Request-Id': 'req_8a7f9c2b'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-small', input: 'hello', max_tokens: 10 })
  })
  console.log(res.status, await res.text())
})()
```

Go (net/http):
```
package main

import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)

func main() {
  apiKey := os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
  body := []byte(`{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hello","max_tokens":10}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate", bytes.NewBuffer(body))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiKey)
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  req.Header.Set("X-Request-Id", "req_8a7f9c2b")
  resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
  if err != nil { panic(err) }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  fmt.Println("status:", resp.Status)
}
```

maya_sre: Add these collection steps for the customer before they run the repro: set LOG_LEVEL=debug on their client, capture the outgoing request bytes (tcpdump or built-in SDK logger), and run the redwood debug collector with the request id. Example: `redwood-debug collect --request-id req_8a7f9c2b --include-logs --include-traces` — this will produce a zip. If they can't run the collector, at minimum paste the full verbose curl output (-v) including headers and response.

rafael_oncall: Also ask them to capture the X-Amzn-Trace-Id or any vendor trace header — if they have a custom gateway, include that header. If we see a 401 and 502 with the same request id, we need the client-side retry behavior and the exact timestamps (to match to infra logs).

anya_engineer: One more tip: if they are using an SDK and rotating keys, ask them to run a short script that hits /v1/models (safe endpoint) to confirm key consistency, then /v1/generate. That helps isolate auth vs routing.

leo_support: I ran the collector command and uploaded the bundle here: https://support-uploads.redwood-internal/s/bugs/2146321987/debug-bundle-req_8a7f9c2b.zip. Customer confirmed they ran the Python snippet and saw 502 then a 401 about 30s later; they provided the second request id: req_8a7f9c2c.

rafael_oncall: Received link, taking the handoff. I'll correlate req_8a7f9c2b/c with infra logs and post back ETA. Thanks for the snippets, @anya_engineer, that should make repro straightforward.
